{{Short description|Method for finding the exact solution of certain quantum mechanics models}}
{{Technical|date=February 2020}}

In [[physics]], the '''Bethe ansatz''' is used to calculate the exact [[Wave function|wave functions]] of certain quantum-mechanical many-body systems, most commonly in one spatial dimension. This [[ansatz]] was introduced by [[Hans Bethe]] in 1931 to obtain the exact [[eigenvalues and eigenvectors]] of the one-dimensional [[Antiferromagnetism|antiferromagnetic]] isotropic (XXX) [[Quantum Heisenberg model|Heisenberg model]].<ref name="1931_Bethe_ZP_71">{{cite journal |last1=Bethe |first1=H. |title=Zur Theorie der Metalle. I. Eigenwerte und Eigenfunktionen der linearen Atomkette |journal=Zeitschrift für Physik |date=March 1931 |volume=71 |issue=3–4 |pages=205–226 |doi=10.1007/BF01341708 |s2cid=124225487}}</ref>

The approach was later generalized into the [[quantum inverse scattering method]] (QISM) and the [[algebraic Bethe ansatz]], forming the basis of modern [[integrable system]] theory.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Korepin |first1=V. E. |last2=Bogoliubov |first2=N. M. |last3=Izergin |first3=A. G. |title=Quantum Inverse Scattering Method and Correlation Functions |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1993 |isbn=978-0-521-37320-3}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Chari |first1=V. |last2=Pressley |first2=A. |title=A Guide to Quantum Groups |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1994 |isbn=978-0-521-55884-6}}</ref>

Since then, the method has been extended to other [[spin chain]]s, statistical [[lattice model (physics)|lattice models]] and [[generalized hydrodynamics]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1=Doyon   | first1=Benjamin
 | title=Lecture notes on Generalised Hydrodynamics
 | journal=SciPost Physics Lecture Notes
 | pages=18
 | year=2020
 | doi=10.21468/SciPostPhysLectNotes.18
  | doi-access=free| url=https://scipost.org/10.21468/SciPostPhysLectNotes.18
| arxiv=1912.08496
 }}</ref>

"Bethe ansatz problems" were one of the topics featuring in the "To learn" section of [[Richard Feynman]]'s blackboard at the time of his death.<ref name="feynman blackboard">{{cite web |title=Richard Feynman's blackboard at time of his death {{!}} Caltech Archives |url=https://digital.archives.caltech.edu/islandora/object/image%3A2545 |website=digital.archives.caltech.edu |access-date=29 July 2023}}</ref>

==Discussion==
In the framework of many-body [[quantum mechanics]], models solvable by the Bethe ansatz can be contrasted with free [[fermion]] models. The dynamics of a free model is one-body reducible: its many-body wave function for [[fermion]]s ([[boson]]s) is the antisymmetrized (symmetrized) product of one-body wave functions. Models solvable by the Bethe ansatz are interacting systems: their two-body sector has a nontrivial [[S-matrix|scattering matrix]] that depends on the particle momenta.

By contrast, such models are two-body reducible: the many-body scattering matrix factorizes into a product of two-body scattering matrices. Many-body collisions occur as sequences of pairwise interactions, and the total wave function can be represented entirely in terms of two-body scattering states. The overall scattering matrix equals the ordered product of these pairwise matrices.

:<math>
\Psi_M(j_1, \cdots, j_M) = \prod_{M \geq a > b \geq 1} \operatorname{sgn}(j_a - j_b) \sum_{P \in \mathfrak S_M} (-1)^{[P]} \exp \left(i \sum_{a=1}^M k_{P_a} j_a + \frac{i}{2}\sum_{M \geq a > b \geq 1} \operatorname{sgn}(j_a - j_b) \phi(k_{P_a}, k_{P_b})\right),
</math> 
where <math>M</math> is the number of particles, <math>j_a\ (a = 1, \cdots M)</math> are their position, <math>\mathfrak S_M</math> is the set of all permutations of the integers <math>1, \cdots, M</math>; <math>(-1)^{[P]} = \pm 1</math> is the parity of the permutation <math>P</math>; <math>k_a</math> is the (quasi-)momentum of the <math>a</math>-th particle, <math>\phi</math> is the scattering phase shift function and <math>\operatorname{sgn}</math> is the [[sign function]]. This form is universal (at least for non-nested systems), with the momentum and scattering functions being model-dependent.

The [[Yang–Baxter equation]] guarantees consistency of the construction.<ref>{{cite book |last=Baxter |first=R. J. |title=Exactly Solved Models in Statistical Mechanics |publisher=Academic Press |year=1982 |isbn=978-0-12-083180-7}}</ref> The [[Pauli exclusion principle]] is valid for models solvable by the Bethe ansatz, even for models of interacting [[bosons]].

The [[ground state]] is a [[Fermi surface|Fermi sphere]]. [[Periodic boundary conditions]] lead to the Bethe ansatz equations or simply Bethe equations. In logarithmic form the Bethe ansatz equations can be generated by the [[Chen-Ning Yang|Yang]] action. The square of the norm of Bethe wave function is equal to the [[determinant]] of the [[Hessian matrix|Hessian]] of the Yang action.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Korepin |first=Vladimir E. |author-link=Vladimir Korepin |date=1982 |title=Calculation of norms of Bethe wave functions |url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1103921777 |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=86 |issue=3 |pages=391–418 |issn=0010-3616 |doi=10.1007/BF01212176 |bibcode=1982CMaPh..86..391K |s2cid=122250890}}</ref>


A substantial generalization is the [[quantum inverse scattering method]], or algebraic Bethe ansatz, which gives an ansatz for the underlying [[operator algebra]] that "has allowed a wide class of nonlinear evolution equations to be solved".<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kaZ0pKIHhxAC&q=quantum+inverse+scattering+method |title=Quantum Inverse Scattering Method and Correlation Functions |last1=Korepin |first1=V. E. |last2=Bogoliubov |first2=N. M. |last3=Izergin |first3=A. G. |date=1997-03-06 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-58646-7 |language=en}}</ref>

The exact solutions of the so-called ''s-d'' model (by P.&nbsp;B.&nbsp;Wiegmann<ref>{{cite journal |title=Exact solution of ''s-d'' exchange model at ''T'' = 0 |author-first1=P. B. |author-last1=Wiegmann |author-link1=Paul Wiegmann |journal=JETP Letters |volume=31 |issue=7 |page=364 |year=1980 |url=http://www.jetpletters.ac.ru/ps/1353/article_20434.pdf |access-date=2019-05-17 |archive-date=2019-05-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190517232654/http://www.jetpletters.ac.ru/ps/1353/article_20434.pdf }}</ref> in 1980 and independently by N.&nbsp;Andrei,<ref name="Andrei1980">{{cite journal |last1=Andrei |first1=N. |title=Diagonalization of the Kondo Hamiltonian |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=45 |issue=5 |year=1980 |pages=379–382 |issn=0031-9007 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.379 |bibcode=1980PhRvL..45..379A}}</ref> also in 1980) and the Anderson model (by P.&nbsp;B.&nbsp;Wiegmann<ref name="Wiegmann1980">{{cite journal |last1=Wiegmann |first1=P. B. |title=Towards an exact solution of the Anderson model |journal=Physics Letters A |volume=80 |issue=2–3 |year=1980 |pages=163–167 |issn=0375-9601 |doi=10.1016/0375-9601(80)90212-1 |bibcode=1980PhLA...80..163W}}</ref> in 1981, and by N.&nbsp;Kawakami and A.&nbsp;Okiji<ref name="KawakamiOkiji1981">{{cite journal |last1=Kawakami |first1=Norio |last2=Okiji |first2=Ayao |title=Exact expression of the ground-state energy for the symmetric anderson model |journal=Physics Letters A |volume=86 |issue=9 |year=1981 |pages=483–486 |issn=0375-9601 |doi=10.1016/0375-9601(81)90663-0 |bibcode=1981PhLA...86..483K}}</ref> in 1981) are also both based on the Bethe ansatz. There exist multi-channel generalizations of these two models also amenable to exact solutions (by N.&nbsp;Andrei and C.&nbsp;Destri<ref name="AndreiDestri1984">{{cite journal |last1=Andrei |first1=N. |last2=Destri |first2=C. |title=Solution of the Multichannel Kondo Problem |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=52 |issue=5 |year=1984 |pages=364–367 |issn=0031-9007 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.364 |bibcode=1984PhRvL..52..364A}}</ref> and by C.&nbsp;J.&nbsp;Bolech and N.&nbsp;Andrei<ref name="BolechAndrei2002">{{cite journal |last1=Bolech |first1=C. J. |last2=Andrei |first2=N. |title=Solution of the Two-Channel Anderson Impurity Model: Implications for the Heavy Fermion UBe<sub>13</sub> |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=88 |issue=23 |year=2002 |article-number=237206 |issn=0031-9007 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.88.237206 |pmid=12059396 |arxiv=cond-mat/0204392 |bibcode=2002PhRvL..88w7206B |s2cid=15180985}}</ref>). Recently several models solvable by Bethe ansatz were realized experimentally in solid states and optical lattices. An important role in the theoretical description of these experiments was played by Jean-Sébastien Caux and [[Alexei Tsvelik]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2018}}

== Terminology ==
There are many similar methods which come under the name of Bethe ansatz
* Algebraic Bethe ansatz.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Faddeev |first1=Ludwig |title=How Algebraic Bethe Ansatz works for integrable model |year=1992 |eprint=hep-th/9605187 }}</ref> The [[quantum inverse scattering method]] is the method of solution by algebraic Bethe ansatz, and the two are practically synonymous.
* Analytic Bethe ansatz
* Coordinate Bethe ansatz {{harvs|last=Bethe|first=Hans|authorlink=Hans Bethe|year=1931}}
* Functional Bethe ansatz<ref>{{cite book |last1=Sklyanin |first1=E. K. |chapter=The quantum Toda chain |title=Non-Linear Equations in Classical and Quantum Field Theory |series=Lecture Notes in Physics |date=1985 |volume=226 |pages=196–233 |doi=10.1007/3-540-15213-X_80|bibcode=1985LNP...226..196S |isbn=978-3-540-15213-2 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Sklyanin |first1=E. K. |title=Integrable and Superintegrable Systems |chapter=Functional Bethe Ansatz |date=October 1990 |pages=8–33 |doi=10.1142/9789812797179_0002|isbn=978-981-02-0316-0 }}</ref>
* Nested Bethe ansatz
* Thermodynamic Bethe ansatz {{harvs|last1=Yang|last2=Yang|first1=C. N.|first2=C. P.|year=1969}}

== Examples ==
=== Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain ===
{{unsourced section|date=February 2025}}
The Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain is defined by the Hamiltonian (assuming periodic boundary conditions)
:<math>
 H = J \sum_{j=1}^N \mathbf{S}_j \cdot \mathbf{S}_{j+1}, \quad \mathbf{S}_{j+N} \equiv \mathbf{S}_j.
</math>

This model is solvable using the (coordinate) Bethe ansatz. The scattering phase shift function is <math>\phi\big(k_a(\lambda_a), k_b(\lambda_b)\big) = \theta_2(\lambda_a - \lambda_b)</math> with <math>\theta_n(\lambda) \equiv 2 \arctan(2\lambda/n),</math> in which the momentum has been conveniently reparametrized as <math>k(\lambda) = \pi - 2 \arctan 2\lambda</math> in terms of the ''rapidity'' <math>\lambda.</math> The boundary conditions (periodic here) impose the ''Bethe equations''
:<math>
 \left[\frac{\lambda_a + i/2}{\lambda_a - i/2}\right]^N =
 \prod_{b \neq a}^M \frac{\lambda_a - \lambda_b + i}{\lambda_a - \lambda_b - i}, \quad a = 1, \dots, M,
</math>
or more conveniently in logarithmic form
:<math>
 \theta_1(\lambda_a) - \frac{1}{N} \sum_{b = 1}^M \theta_2(\lambda_a - \lambda_b) = 2\pi \frac{I_a}{N},
</math>
where the quantum numbers <math>I_j</math> are distinct half-odd integers for <math>N - M</math> even, integers for <math>N - M</math> odd (with <math>I_j</math> defined <math>\bmod N</math>).

== Applicability ==
The following systems can be solved using the Bethe ansatz
* [[Anderson impurity model]]
* [[Gaudin model]]
* XXX and XXZ [[Heisenberg spin chain]] for arbitrary spin <math>s</math>
* [[Hubbard model]]
* [[Kondo model]]
* [[Lieb–Liniger model]]
* [[Six-vertex model]] and [[Eight-vertex model]] (through Heisenberg spin chain)

==Chronology==
{{Prose|section|date=February 2020}}
* 1928: [[Werner Heisenberg]] publishes [[Quantum Heisenberg model|his model]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Heisenberg |first1=W. |title=Zur Theorie des Ferromagnetismus |journal=Zeitschrift für Physik |date=September 1928 |volume=49 |issue=9–10 |pages=619–636 |doi=10.1007/BF01328601|bibcode=1928ZPhy...49..619H |s2cid=122524239 }}</ref>
* 1930: [[Felix Bloch]] proposes an oversimplified ansatz which miscounts the number of solutions to the Schrödinger equation for the Heisenberg chain.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bloch |first1=F. |title=Zur Theorie des Ferromagnetismus |journal=Zeitschrift für Physik |date=March 1930 |volume=61 |issue=3–4 |pages=206–219 |doi=10.1007/BF01339661|bibcode=1930ZPhy...61..206B |s2cid=120459635 }}</ref>
* 1931: [[Hans Bethe]] proposes the correct ansatz and carefully shows that it yields the correct number of eigenfunctions.<ref name="1931_Bethe_ZP_71"/>
* 1938: {{Interlanguage link|Lamek Hulthén|de}} obtains the exact ground-state energy of the Heisenberg model.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hulthén |first1=Lamek |title=Über das Austauschproblem eines Kristalles |journal=Arkiv Mat. Astron. Fysik |date=1938 |volume=26A |page=1}}</ref>
* 1958: [[Raymond Lee Orbach]] uses the Bethe ansatz to solve the Heisenberg model with anisotropic interactions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Orbach |first1=R. |title=Linear Antiferromagnetic Chain with Anisotropic Coupling |journal=Physical Review |date=15 October 1958 |volume=112 |issue=2 |pages=309–316 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.112.309|bibcode=1958PhRv..112..309O }}</ref>
* 1962: J. des Cloizeaux and J. J. Pearson obtain the correct spectrum of the Heisenberg antiferromagnet (spinon dispersion relation),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=des Cloizeaux |first1=Jacques |last2=Pearson |first2=J. J. |title=Spin-Wave Spectrum of the Antiferromagnetic Linear Chain |journal=Physical Review |date=1 December 1962 |volume=128 |issue=5 |pages=2131–2135 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.128.2131|bibcode=1962PhRv..128.2131D }}</ref> showing that it differs from Anderson's spin-wave theory predictions<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Anderson |first1=P. W. |title=An Approximate Quantum Theory of the Antiferromagnetic Ground State |journal=Physical Review |date=1 June 1952 |volume=86 |issue=5 |pages=694–701 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.86.694|bibcode=1952PhRv...86..694A }}</ref> (the constant prefactor is different).
* 1963: [[Elliott H. Lieb]] and {{ill|Werner Liniger|de}} provide the exact solution of the 1d δ-function interacting Bose gas<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lieb |first1=Elliott H. |last2=Liniger |first2=Werner |title=Exact Analysis of an Interacting Bose Gas. I. The General Solution and the Ground State |journal=Physical Review |date=15 May 1963 |volume=130 |issue=4 |pages=1605–1616 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.130.1605|bibcode=1963PhRv..130.1605L }}</ref> (now known as the [[Lieb-Liniger model]]). Lieb studies the spectrum and defines two basic types of excitations.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lieb |first1=Elliott H. |title=Exact Analysis of an Interacting Bose Gas. II. The Excitation Spectrum |journal=Physical Review |date=15 May 1963 |volume=130 |issue=4 |pages=1616–1624 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.130.1616|bibcode=1963PhRv..130.1616L }}</ref>
* 1964: [[Robert B. Griffiths]] obtains the magnetization curve of the Heisenberg model at zero temperature.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Griffiths |first1=Robert B. |title=Magnetization Curve at Zero Temperature for the Antiferromagnetic Heisenberg Linear Chain |journal=Physical Review |date=3 February 1964 |volume=133 |issue=3A |pages=A768–A775 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.133.A768|bibcode=1964PhRv..133..768G }}</ref>
* 1966: [[Yang Chen-Ning|C. N. Yang]] and [[C. P. Yang]] rigorously prove that the ground-state of the Heisenberg chain is given by the Bethe ansatz.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yang |first1=C. N. |last2=Yang |first2=C. P. |title=One-Dimensional Chain of Anisotropic Spin-Spin Interactions. I. Proof of Bethe's Hypothesis for Ground State in a Finite System |journal=Physical Review |date=7 October 1966 |volume=150 |issue=1 |pages=321–327 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.150.321|bibcode=1966PhRv..150..321Y }}</ref> They study properties and applications in<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yang |first1=C. N. |last2=Yang |first2=C. P. |title=One-Dimensional Chain of Anisotropic Spin-Spin Interactions. II. Properties of the Ground-State Energy Per Lattice Site for an Infinite System |journal=Physical Review |date=7 October 1966 |volume=150 |issue=1 |pages=327–339 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.150.327|bibcode=1966PhRv..150..327Y }}</ref> and.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yang |first1=C. N. |last2=Yang |first2=C. P. |title=One-Dimensional Chain of Anisotropic Spin-Spin Interactions. III. Applications |journal=Physical Review |date=4 November 1966 |volume=151 |issue=1 |pages=258–264 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.151.258|bibcode=1966PhRv..151..258Y }}</ref>
* 1967: [[Yang Chen-Ning|C. N. Yang]] generalizes Lieb and Liniger's solution of the δ-function interacting Bose gas to arbitrary permutation symmetry of the wavefunction, giving birth to the nested Bethe ansatz.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yang |first1=C. N. |title=Some Exact Results for the Many-Body Problem in one Dimension with Repulsive Delta-Function Interaction |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=4 December 1967 |volume=19 |issue=23 |pages=1312–1315 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.19.1312|bibcode=1967PhRvL..19.1312Y |url=http://edoc.hu-berlin.de/18452/20513 }}</ref>
* 1968: [[Elliott H. Lieb]] and [[Fa-Yueh Wu|F. Y. Wu]] solve the 1d Hubbard model.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lieb |first1=Elliott H. |last2=Wu |first2=F. Y. |title=Absence of Mott Transition in an Exact Solution of the Short-Range, One-Band Model in One Dimension |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=17 June 1968 |volume=20 |issue=25 |pages=1445–1448 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.20.1445|bibcode=1968PhRvL..20.1445L }}</ref>
* 1969: [[Yang Chen-Ning|C. N. Yang]] and [[C. P. Yang]] obtain the thermodynamics of the Lieb-Liniger model,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Yang |first1=C. N. |last2=Yang |first2=C. P. |title=Thermodynamics of a One-Dimensional System of Bosons with Repulsive Delta-Function Interaction |journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics |date=July 1969 |volume=10 |issue=7 |pages=1115–1122 |doi=10.1063/1.1664947|bibcode=1969JMP....10.1115Y }}</ref> providing the basis of the thermodynamic Bethe ansatz (TBA).
